objective: Theory spec of Gaussian-ansatz TMDs at leading order without evolution (SIDIS F_UU,T, Cahn, Sivers, Drell-Yan q_T, Sivers sign change) in theory:tmd-gaussian-lo

model.description: Gaussian-ansatz TMD distribution and fragmentation functions with constant, flavour-independent widths, at leading order in alpha_s and without evolution: SIDIS F_UU,T with <P_T^2> = <p_perp^2> + z^2 <k_perp^2>, the Cahn cos(phi_h) term at O(k/Q), the Sivers asymmetry in the Gaussian Sivers model, the Drell-Yan q_T shape with <q_T^2> = <k1^2> + <k2^2>, and the SIDIS -> Drell-Yan Sivers sign change

assumptions: Gaussian k_perp and p_perp dependence, constant flavour-independent widths (Anselmino et al. Eqs. 34-35): a model, so the physics status is heuristic-argument
P_hT = z k_perp + p_perp, x = x_B, z = z_h at O(k_perp/Q) (Eq. 29); Cahn term kept at O(k_perp/Q)
Sivers function 2 N_q(x) h'(k) f(x, k), h' = sqrt(2e)(k/M') exp(-k^2/M'^2) (Eqs. 63, 68)
Drell-Yan q_T: tree-level convolution of two Gaussian TMD PDFs, no soft factor

conventions.unit_system: natural-HEP: transverse momenta in GeV, Gaussian widths <k_perp^2>, <p_perp^2>, M'^2 in GeV^2; F_UU,T and the q_T shape per GeV^2; asymmetries dimensionless
conventions.coupling_normalization: alpha_s = g_s^2/(4 pi); not used: leading order in alpha_s, no alpha_s-dependent factor
conventions.em_coupling: alpha = e^2/(4 pi) enters only common prefactors (2 pi alpha^2 ...) that cancel in the shapes and ratios; no value of alpha is used
conventions.scales: not-applicable (no TMD evolution: widths are constants, independent of Q^2, x, z and flavour)
conventions.energy_variable: SIDIS: x_B, Q^2, y, z_h, P_hT (hadron transverse momentum relative to the virtual photon); Drell-Yan: dilepton q_T
conventions.frame: SIDIS: gamma* - nucleon frame (Trento conventions): virtual photon along +z, nucleon P = P0(1, 0, 0, -1), incoming lepton l = E(1, sin theta, 0, cos theta) with a positive x component, lepton plane = x-z plane (Anselmino et al. p. 2); any frame reached from the target rest frame by a boost along q-hat; Drell-Yan: hadronic centre-of-mass frame for q_T
conventions.angle_definition: phi_h, phi_S: azimuths of P_hT and S_T about the photon axis, measured from the lepton plane; phi: azimuth of the quark k_perp
conventions.spin_treatment: unpolarized for F_UU,T, the Cahn term and Drell-Yan q_T; transversely polarized nucleon (S_T) for the Sivers term
conventions.mass_approximation: massless partons; target and hadron masses neglected (gamma = 2Mx/Q -> 0 in Bacchetta et al. Eqs. 2.8-2.11)
conventions.exchanged_bosons: photon only (one-photon exchange in SIDIS; virtual photon in Drell-Yan)
conventions.factorization_scheme: not-applicable (tree-level TMD parton model, no evolution or soft factor)
conventions.polarization_convention: Sivers function: Delta^N f_{q/p^up}(x, k) S_T . (P-hat x k-hat) (Anselmino et al. Eqs. 48-50) = -(2|k_T|/M) f_1T^perp (x, k_T^2) (Trento Eq. 4); Drell-Yan f_1T^perp = - SIDIS f_1T^perp (Trento Eq. 14)
conventions.azimuth_convention: Trento conventions (Trento Eq. 16; Bacchetta et al. Eq. 2.3) for phi_h and phi_S. Anselmino et al. use the same angles: with l_x > 0, P_T = P_T(cos phi_h, sin phi_h, 0) and S_T = |S_T|(cos phi_S, sin phi_S, 0) (pp. 2, 6, 11), Trento Eq. 16 gives cos phi_h and sin phi_h unchanged (mapping in derivations/derivation-record.md, step 5)
conventions.tmdg:gaussian_ansatz: f_q(x, k) = f_q(x) exp(-k^2/<k_perp^2>)/(pi <k_perp^2>), D_q(z, p) = D_q(z) exp(-p^2/<p_perp^2>)/(pi <p_perp^2>), p = hadron transverse momentum relative to the fragmenting quark, P_hT = z k + p at O(k/Q) (Anselmino et al. Eqs. 29, 34-35); constant, flavour-independent widths
conventions.tmdg:fragmentation_normalization: Anselmino: int d^2p D(z, p) = D(z) (Eq. 37). Bacchetta: D_1(z) = z^2 int d^2k_T D_1(z, k_T^2), k_T the quark relative to the hadron, hadron relative to quark = -z k_T (Eq. 3.41), so <p_perp^2> = z^2 <k_T^2>

extension.order: leading order in alpha_s; leading power in k_perp/Q for F_UU,T, the Sivers term and Drell-Yan, O(k_perp/Q) for the Cahn term; no TMD evolution

parameters.widths_note: fitted values of Anselmino et al. (Eq. 47, Table I) used as ILLUSTRATIVE settings; collinear values, N_q and Drell-Yan widths SYNTHETIC

validity_domain.kinematics: P_hT ~ k_perp << Q (the paper's validity statement: corrections O(k_perp^2/Q^2) small); no matching to the large-P_hT collinear region
validity_domain.model: constant Gaussian widths independent of x, z, Q^2 and flavour; no evolution; the derivations are exact within this model (analytic-derivation per step in derivations/derivation.json)
validity_domain.sivers_sign: applies to TMDs with the SIDIS and Drell-Yan Wilson lines (Trento Eq. 14)

checks_run.name: Gaussian normalizations, including D_1(z) = z^2 int d^2k_T D_1(z, k_T^2) (SymPy)
SIDIS convolution gives the Gaussian in P_hT with <P_T^2> = <p_perp^2> + z^2 <k_perp^2> (Anselmino form) and the same F_UU,T from the Bacchetta convolution with <p_perp^2> = z^2 <k_T^2> (SymPy)
d^2P_hT integral of F_UU,T = x sum e^2 f D (Bacchetta Eq. 4.21) (SymPy and numerical)
Eq. 32 with Eq. 33 reproduces the Cahn term of Eq. 38; Bacchetta Eq. 4.20 with Eqs. 2.9 and 2.11 at gamma = 0 gives the same bracket (SymPy)
Eq. 58 with Eqs. 63, 68 reproduces Eqs. 64-67; Bacchetta Eq. 4.11 with Trento Eq. 4 gives the same asymmetry (SymPy)
Drell-Yan: two Gaussians convolve to width <k1^2> + <k2^2>, unit normalization (SymPy and numerical)
Trento Eq. 4 round trip between Delta^N f and f_1T^perp (SymPy); the Drell-Yan sign (Trento Eq. 14) is applied as a cited rule, not checked
closed forms against 2D adaptive quadrature of the defining integrals (toy inputs)

published closed forms (Anselmino et al. Eqs. 38-39 and 64-67) against the profile's quadrature of its transcription of the same integrands at 4 (z, P_T) points (same route as the paper: checks algebra and transcription, not physics)
frame map: Anselmino et al. (q along +z, P along -z, l_x > 0; pp. 2, 6, 11) inserted in Trento Eq. 16 gives the same phi_h and phi_S (by hand, recorded in derivation-record.md)
limits: Cahn ratio 1 and Sivers asymmetry 0 at P_hT = 0

checks_not_run: TMD evolution, the soft factor and the matching to collinear factorization at large P_hT
an independent derivation of the Sivers sign change (cited from the Trento conventions)
a Drell-Yan Sivers asymmetry formula: no source read gives one, so only the sign of the Sivers function is propagated
comparison with measured multiplicities, asymmetries or q_T spectra

references_read.citation: M. Anselmino, M. Boglione, U. D'Alesio, A. Kotzinian, F. Murgia, A. Prokudin, 'The role of Cahn and Sivers effects in deep inelastic scattering', arXiv:hep-ph/0501196v2
A. Bacchetta, M. Diehl, K. Goeke, A. Metz, P.J. Mulders, M. Schlegel, 'Semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering at small transverse momentum', arXiv:hep-ph/0611265v2
A. Bacchetta, U. D'Alesio, M. Diehl, C.A. Miller, 'Single-spin asymmetries: the Trento conventions', arXiv:hep-ph/0410050v2

neglected: flavour, x and z dependence of the widths
